skill.name: cosmic-database
skill.description: Download authenticated COSMIC cancer genomics files and guide analysis of mutations, cancer genes, signatures, fusions, copy number, expression, and resistance data.
skill.summary: Access and analyze licensed COSMIC cancer genomics datasets with authenticated downloads and practical Python workflows.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most detections are false positives from Markdown formatting, documentation URLs, local VCF access, and expected downloader behavior. The endpoint-supplied download URL is fetched without validation, and the CLI permits passwords in process arguments. No prompt injection or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: The API-provided download URL is fetched without destination validation.
remediation.suggestion: Require HTTPS and allow only documented COSMIC download hosts before requesting the returned URL. Reject credentials, redirects, private addresses, and unexpected schemes.

remediation.issue: The --password option can expose credentials through process arguments and shell history.
remediation.suggestion: Remove command-line password input and always use getpass or a protected credential provider. Document secure noninteractive authentication if COSMIC supports it.

content.value_statement: Cancer genomics teams need reliable access to licensed COSMIC datasets and clear analysis patterns. This skill provides authenticated downloads, file guidance, and practical workflows.
actual_capabilities: Downloads authenticated COSMIC files through the official download endpoint.
Maps common data types to COSMIC file paths for GRCh37 or GRCh38.
Supports mutation, gene census, resistance, structural variant, expression, copy number, fusion, signature, and sample files.
Shows pandas and pysam workflows for filtering tabular and VCF data.
Explains COSMIC file formats, field meanings, release versions, and licensing requirements.
limitations: Requires a valid COSMIC account and may require a commercial license.
Does not provide COSMIC data without authentication or bypass access controls.
Downloads can consume several gigabytes of storage and substantial network time.
Examples support research workflows and do not provide clinical decisions.

use_cases.title: Explore Cancer Mutations
use_cases.description: Download mutation datasets and filter records by gene, tumor site, or genomic region.

use_cases.title: Build Reproducible Data Pipelines
use_cases.description: Pin assemblies and releases while integrating COSMIC files into validated analysis pipelines.

use_cases.title: Review Cancer Gene Evidence
use_cases.description: Use gene census, resistance, fusion, and signature resources to support research interpretation.

prompt_templates.title: Download the Gene Census
prompt_templates.prompt: Download the latest GRCh38 Cancer Gene Census to {output_path}. Ask before network access and avoid exposing my COSMIC password.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize Gene Mutations
prompt_templates.prompt: Using {mutation_file}, summarize {gene} mutations for {cancer_type}. Report counts, key fields, assembly, and data release.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Mutational Signatures
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a reproducible workflow to compare SBS signatures in {dataset}. Pin the COSMIC release and list required inputs and validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Multi-Source Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a pipeline combining COSMIC mutations, structural variants, and resistance data for {cohort}. Include licensing, provenance, validation, and secure credential handling.

output_examples.input: Find the current GRCh38 path for the Cancer Gene Census.
output_examples.output: Use GRCh38/cosmic/latest/cancer_gene_census.csv. Pin a numbered release instead of latest when reproducibility is required.

output_examples.input: Summarize TP53 records from a downloaded mutation table.
output: Dataset: COSMIC mutation export, with assembly and release reported.
Summary: record count, primary sites, mutation types, and source identifiers.

output_examples.output: Confirm licensing, prompt for the password privately, validate the COSMIC destination, verify disk space, and record the release and checksum.

best_practices: Pin a COSMIC release and genome assembly for reproducible research.
Prompt for credentials securely and confirm network access before downloading.
Record source paths, release details, checksums, filters, and licensing terms.
anti_patterns: Do not place passwords in prompts, source files, command arguments, or notebooks.
Do not mix GRCh37 and GRCh38 coordinates without an explicit validated conversion.
Do not use COSMIC research data as an independent clinical diagnosis or treatment recommendation.

faq.question: Does this skill include COSMIC data?
faq.answer: No. It provides download and analysis guidance. You must obtain data through your authorized COSMIC account.

faq.question: Do I need a COSMIC account?
faq.answer: Yes. Academic access requires registration, and commercial use may require a QIAGEN license.

faq.question: Which genome assemblies are supported?
faq.answer: The helper supports GRCh37 and GRCh38. GRCh38 is the recommended current assembly.

faq.question: Can I select a fixed COSMIC release?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide a numbered version instead of latest to improve reproducibility.

faq.question: Which file formats can I analyze?
faq.answer: The guidance covers compressed TSV, CSV, and VCF files using pandas or pysam.

faq.question: Is this suitable for clinical decisions?
faq.answer: No. It supports cancer research workflows and requires independent clinical validation for patient care.
